cells.title: Add the one-line worker status digest and move progress notes to progress.jsonl
cells.action: Write the red test FIRST and watch it fail: `bee herding status --job J` on a mailbox with job.json and a log.txt holding a sentinel string but no progress.jsonl and no result file prints exactly `no progress notes yet` (JSON: {job, line, source: none, notes: 0}), exits 0, and the sentinel never appears in the output. Then build. (1) notify.rs: `--kind progress` appends one line {ts, step, note} to `.bee/mailbox/<job>/progress.jsonl` (add `progress_path` in mailbox.rs beside messages/result paths), never to messages.jsonl; `--step` optional; a note over 120 characters is refused with a FIX; `--job <id>` overrides BEE_HERDING_JOB_ID and, for progress only, needs no job.json (it creates the job dir); the job-id path checks stay. Every other kind keeps today's messages.jsonl behaviour byte for byte, and the internal stall alert (herding.rs, search `no_diff_progress for`) keeps writing to messages.jsonl. (2) New module herding/status_digest.rs, wired from the existing `status` verb when `--job` is present (no `--job` keeps today's fleet output unchanged). It reads ONLY progress.jsonl and the highest result-N.json (reuse mailbox's latest_result_round); a torn last line is skipped. Order: result file → `<status>: <summary>` (source result); no notes → `no progress notes yet` (source none); notes ≤ 3 → last note verbatim as `<step>: <note>` or `<note>` (source verbatim); notes > 3 → if status-digest.json holds the same note count, its line (source cached); else ask the supervisor and cache {notes, line, at} (source supervisor); any failure → last note verbatim (source verbatim, plus `fallback` reason in JSON). The supervisor call runs this same binary's `dispatch prepare --runtime <rt> --kind gather --role supervisor --json` (rt: the runtime the dispatch door detects, claude when unknown) and runs the returned payload only when tool is Bash, passing on stdin a task that holds the notes and asks for one status line; take the first non-empty line of the result summary, cut to 120 chars. A non-Bash payload means no supervisor. Put the call behind a trait or fn seam so tests inject a fake summarizer and never reach paseo. (3) mailbox.rs render_brief: add one short paragraph telling a herded worker to append one JSON line {"ts","step","note"} (note ≤120 chars) to the absolute progress.jsonl path at each meaningful step, either by hand or with notify --kind progress; keep the notify line. (4) generated/registry_payload.json: if it describes `herding status` or `herding notify`, add --job / --step there (hand-maintained). Tests (behaviour, not structure): the red test above; ≤3 notes → last note verbatim and the fake summarizer is never called; result-2.json present → result line wins; 4 notes + fake summarizer → source supervisor and status-digest.json written, a second call → source cached and the fake not called again; 4 notes + failing summarizer → verbatim fallback; notify --kind progress writes progress.jsonl and leaves messages.jsonl absent; a 121-char note refused; notify --kind progress --job X with no job.json succeeds; notify --kind blocked still writes messages.jsonl. Update existing tests that assert progress lands in messages.jsonl (notify.rs tests near `half done`, herding.rs near line 2226 and 3222) to the new contract, citing decision 28b87b5b. No code comments.

truths: bee herding status --job J with no progress.jsonl and no result prints `no progress notes yet` and exits 0, and never prints log.txt content
With 3 or fewer notes the line is the last note verbatim and no model is called
A result-N.json outranks notes
With more than 3 notes the supervisor line is used and cached by note count; failure falls back to the last note verbatim
bee herding notify --kind progress writes progress.jsonl only, refuses a note over 120 characters, and accepts --job with no job.json
Other notify kinds and the stall alert still write messages.jsonl
bee herding status with no --job is unchanged
The herded brief tells the worker to append progress notes to the absolute progress.jsonl path

(2) skills/bee-swarming/SKILL.md step 4 (Tend): the leader learns a running worker's progress only from `bee herding status --job <id>` — one line — and never reads a worker's transcript, pane log, log.txt or activity stream for progress; cite decision d9007aca. Mirror one sentence in swarming-reference.md where it describes tending or stuck workers (search `Operating Contract in full`), pointing to SKILL.md as the home. (3) packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md § Work in parallel: one bullet — a leader watches a worker through `bee herding status --job <id>` (one line), never by reading its transcript, pane log or activity stream; workers write the notes. Keep it to two lines; it is the doctrine home, the skill text carries the how. (4) docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/the-run-verb-and-worker-outcomes.md: a section `Status digest` with the D4 order (result, none, verbatim ≤3, supervisor >3 with cache, fallback), the sources list, what it never reads, and Pointers to herding/status_digest.rs and herding.rs; add the decisions to the concept's decisions list. the-mailbox-broker.md: progress notes live in progress.jsonl, are never delivered to the leader, and messages.jsonl keeps question/blocked/dependency/reopen and the stall alert (decision 28b87b5b).
